industry: Vehicle wraps, vinyl graphics, and custom signage
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Mitch will confidently give you a price, date, or decision, then almost immediately reconsider, contradict himself, and revise it again (sometimes multiple times in one message thread). He's enthusiastic and apologetic about it ('actually, hang on, scratch that'), but customers often end a conversation with three different answers to the same question and no idea which one is final.
background_facts:
SOUTHSIDE SIGNS & WRAPS — Manukau, Auckland, NZ. Owned by Mitch Reweti since 2015, small shop unit with a two-bay garage.

STAFF: Mitch (owner, head installer, does most quoting himself which is part of the problem), Aroha (part-time front desk/admin, Tue/Thu/Fri), Sione (apprentice installer, 6 months in, still training on complex wraps).

SERVICES & ROUGH PRICING (NZD):
- Full vehicle wrap: $2,800–$4,200 depending on vehicle size/material (van vs hatchback)
- Partial wrap: $900–$1,600
- Vinyl lettering/decals: from $150
- Shop signage (acrylic/lightbox): from $400
- Banners: $80–$250
- Window graphics/frosting: from $180

TURNAROUND: Full wrap 3–5 business days once vehicle is dropped off; lettering usually same/next day; signage about a week, longer if custom lightbox parts need ordering.

HOURS: Mon–Fri 8am–5pm. Closed weekends 'officially,' though Mitch sometimes opens Saturdays by appointment — this policy flip-flops depending on how busy the week was.

DEPOSIT POLICY: Supposed to be 50% deposit to lock in a booking. Mitch frequently waives it for people he likes or regulars, then worries about cashflow later and tries to walk it back.

PAYMENT: Bank transfer preferred, EFTPOS in-store. Credit card surcharge situation is unclear even to Mitch — he thinks he removed the card machine surcharge last year but isn't sure it's updated on the reader.

MATERIALS: Orders 3M and Avery vinyl through a distributor in Penrose; chrome/specialty finishes sometimes go on backorder 1–2 weeks, which throws out timelines Mitch has already promised.

PAIN POINTS: Booking calendar is a shared paper diary plus a phone calendar Aroha doesn't always see — leads to double-bookings. Mitch tends to promise slots verbally without confirming with Aroha first, then has to call back and reschedule.

GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT:
1. Current chrome-wrap material pricing — supplier changed their price list recently and Mitch hasn't finished recalculating what to charge, so any quote involving chrome finish is a guess.
2. Whether Saturday appointments are still viable at all, since Sione (who used to cover some Saturday installs) changed his availability and Mitch hasn't decided if he'll do them solo anymore.
